html:
In 1536 King Christian III arrested the Catholic bishops of Denmark and made the Lutheran church the church of the state. Norway, ruled from Copenhagen, followed.

Lutheran preaching had spread in Danish towns since the 1520s, led by Hans Tausen. A civil war, the Count's Feud, ended with Christian III in power. He seized church lands, which doubled the crown's wealth, and the new church order of 1537 was approved by Luther himself.

The Bible was put into Danish in 1550. In Norway and Iceland the change came mostly from above and met resistance. To this day the Evangelical Lutheran Church is the national church of Denmark and most Danes belong to it. It was part of the wider Reformation, and it bound Denmark-Norway closer to the German Protestant states.
sum: In 1536 King Christian III arrested the Catholic bishops of Denmark and made the Lutheran church the church of the state. Norway, ruled from Copenhagen, followed.
